title: How would you design a recommendation system: start simple (trending/popular, recent activity, category-based rules) before ML, then collaborative filtering (users who liked X also liked Y) vs content-based filtering (similar item attributes), offline precomputation of recommendations vs real-time ranking, event tracking for feedback, and the cold-start problem for new users/items?
shortTitle: How would you design a recommendation system
keyPoints: Start with simple baselines (trending, popular, recent activity, category rules) before any machine learning.
Collaborative filtering recommends based on behavior patterns: users who liked X also liked Y.
Content-based filtering recommends items with similar attributes to what the user already liked.
Offline precomputation generates candidate sets; a lightweight online ranker re-orders with fresh context.
Event tracking (impressions, clicks, conversions) closes the feedback loop for continuous improvement.
Cold-start for new users: popularity plus onboarding signals; for new items: content attributes plus exploratory exposure.
Blend collaborative and content-based into a hybrid; inject exploration to avoid filter bubbles.

s1_definition.oneliner: Start with popularity and rules, add collaborative and content-based filtering, precompute candidates offline and rank in real time, close the loop with event feedback, and handle cold-start with popularity and attributes.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Start simple** – Trending, popular, recent activity, and category rules deliver most value cheaply and serve as the fallback.
- **Collaborative filtering** – Recommends based on behavior patterns: users who liked X also liked Y.
- **Content-based** – Recommends items with similar attributes; works for new items and gives explainable results.
- **Two-stage** – Offline batch precomputes candidate sets; a lightweight online ranker re-orders with fresh context.
- **Feedback loop** – Track impressions, clicks, and conversions to retrain models; A/B test before rolling out.
- **Cold-start** – New users see popular items plus onboarding signals; new items use content attributes.
s1_definition.analogy: When Rajesh logs into National Bank of India's app, it suggests products. The simplest version shows the most popular products this month (trending). A smarter version notices customers like Rajesh often took a home loan (collaborative filtering). Another angle sees Rajesh has a fixed deposit and suggests similar savings products (content-based). The bank prepares suggestions overnight (offline) and re-orders them when Rajesh opens the app (real-time ranking).

sections.s6_takeaway:
Pankaj designs a recommendation system as a layered pipeline of fallbacks and a blend, not a single algorithm. At National Bank of India, he deliberately starts with simple baselines: trending products, popular items, recent activity, and category rules like suggesting a fixed deposit to a savings account customer. These deliver most of the value cheaply, need no training, and give a baseline to beat. ML is added only when these plateau.

The two ML approaches are collaborative filtering (users who liked X also liked Y, using the interaction matrix) and content-based filtering (items with similar attributes to what the user liked, using feature vectors). Collaborative discovers non-obvious connections but suffers from cold-start; content-based works for new items and gives explainable results but stays within what the user already likes. Blending them into a hybrid is what real systems do.

For performance, heavy candidate generation runs in nightly batch to produce a candidate set per user, and a lightweight online ranker re-orders with fresh context at request time. The feedback loop tracks impressions, clicks, and conversions, streams them to a pipeline for training labels, and A/B tests new models before rollout. Cold-start degrades gracefully: new users see popular items plus onboarding signals, new items are placed by content attributes with exploratory exposure.

Remember one sentence: Start with popularity and rules, add collaborative and content-based filtering blended into a hybrid, precompute candidates offline, rank cheaply in real time, close the loop with event tracking and A/B testing, and handle cold-start by degrading from collaborative to content-based to popularity.
